Launch the BirdNET classifier training app

Source: R/birdnet_train_app.R
pam_train_app.Rd

A standalone tool, not a workflow stage: a point-and-click interface for training a custom BirdNET classifier, laid out like the training tab of the BirdNET-Analyzer GUI: training data, cache, frequency and speed, cropping, autotune, training settings and the model save mode. It shows the progress and the learning curves while training runs, can repeat a training several times to show how much the scores vary, keeps a history of earlier runs, and gives the birdnet: config lines that use the trained model.

Usage

pam_train_app(
  cfg = NULL,
  data_dir = NULL,
  output_dir = NULL,
  lang = NULL,
  envdir = pam_birdnet_env_dir("training")
)

Arguments

cfg

Optional configuration from pam_load_config(); its birdnet$model_dir is used as the default output folder.

data_dir

Optional training folder to start with (one sub-folder per class).

output_dir

Optional output folder to start with.

lang

Interface language code (for example "en"). NULL chooses from options(pamflow.lang), the PAMFLOW_LANG variable or the system language, and falls back to English. Translations live in inst/i18n/<code>.yml; a translation only needs the texts it changes.

envdir

Folder of the training Python environment (see pam_birdnet_setup("training")).

Value

A Shiny app object. Printing it at the console starts it, or pass it to shiny::runApp().

Details

This is a standalone tool: it is not a stage of the workflow and no workflow function calls it. Use the trained model by pointing the birdnet: section of the config at it.

Training runs in a separate process, so the app stays responsive and Stop ends the training and everything it started. Closing the app also stops a running training. The settings shown are the BirdNET-Analyzer 2.4.0 defaults; each value you see is the value used, and it is recorded in the run's _run.yml. The first training downloads the base BirdNET model (about 224 MB) once.

The scores shown come from clips held out of the training folder and are therefore optimistic; give a separate test folder for a more honest estimate.

Examples

if (interactive()) {
  pam_train_app()
}
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
pam_train_app(data_dir = "E:/clips", output_dir = "E:/models", lang = "en")
} # }
